title: Microsoft Purview Endpoint DLP: protect unsaved content from printing, USB and network shares
summary: The briefing accurately distinguishes the planned unsaved-content protection from Microsoft's currently documented limitations. The roadmap facts, licensing, existing activity restrictions and PowerShell operation are supported; minor corrections would complete the navigation path and align the checklist with the controls table.

claims.quote: Monitor or protect file with unsaved sensitive content from being printed or being moved to USB or network share.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: The roadmap description names no new identity, permission or sign-in behaviour.
claims.quote: Monitor or protect file with unsaved sensitive content from being printed or being moved to USB or network share.

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: Endpoint DLP extends Microsoft Purview DLP activity monitoring and protection to onboarded Windows and macOS devices.
claims.quote: Endpoint data loss prevention (Endpoint DLP) extends the activity monitoring and protection capabilities of DLP to Windows 10/11, macOS (the three latest released major versions) devices, and Windows certain server versions.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Learn currently states that Endpoint DLP cannot scan or classify data never saved to a file on the local device.
claims.quote: If data is never saved to a file on the local device, Endpoint DLP cannot scan or classify it.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Learn states that saving a document from Word directly to USB without first storing it locally cannot be inspected or blocked by Endpoint DLP.
claims.quote: For example, if a user opens a document in Word and saves it directly to a USB device without first storing it locally, Endpoint DLP cannot inspect or block that action.

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: Learn documents classification of files when they are created or modified.
claims.quote: Creation or Modification: Every time a file is created or modified, it is fully scanned for sensitive information types (SITs) and labels. The file is then evaluated for matches against DLP policies and rules.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; controls[0].note; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Existing Endpoint DLP activity restrictions can audit, warn or block printing protected files.
claims.quote: When this activity is detected, you can block, warn, or audit the printing of protected files from an endpoint device.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; controls[0].note; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Existing Endpoint DLP activity restrictions can audit, warn or block copying or moving protected files to USB removable media.
claims.quote: When this activity is detected, you can block, warn, or audit the copying or moving of protected files from an endpoint device to USB removable media.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; controls[0].note; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Existing Endpoint DLP activity restrictions can audit, warn or block copying or moving protected files to a network share.
claims.quote: When this activity is detected, you can block, warn, or audit the copying or moving of protected files from an endpoint device to any network share

claims.where: Scope: Users and devices; controls[0].note; Governance guidance; rationale: impact
claims.claim: An endpoint DLP policy is enforced on an endpoint only when both the user and the device are in the policy scope.
claims.quote: For a DLP policy to be enforced on an endpoint, both the user and the device must be included in the policy scope.

claims.where: Scope: Roles; Governance controls
claims.claim: EndpointDlpRestrictions requires membership in the Compliance Administrator or Compliance Data Administrator roles in Microsoft Entra ID.
claims.quote: Note: This parameter requires membership in the Compliance Administrator or Compliance Data Administrator roles in Microsoft Entra ID.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The printed Microsoft Purview portal route reaches the device activity restrictions in the custom policy wizard.
claims.quote: Select the Custom from the Categories then Custom policy template from Regulations. ... Select Full directory under Admin units. ... Scope the location to Devices only. ... Select Audit or restrict activities on devices. ... Select Apply restrictions to specific activity
claims.fix: Replace the path with 'Data Loss Prevention > Policies > Create policy > Enterprise applications & devices > Categories > Custom > Regulations > Custom policy > Admin units > Full directory > Devices > rule > Actions > Audit or restrict activities on devices > Apply restrictions to specific activity'. The existing steps are in the documented order; the omitted headings and administrative-scope selection warrant only a minor. The path may end at the restrictions control without reproducing the sample rule's condition.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Set-DlpComplianceRule -Identity "<rule name>" -EndpointDlpRestrictions @{"Setting"="RemovableMedia"; "Value"="Block"} is the documented operation and deciding parameter for blocking USB copying in a DLP rule.
claims.quote: Use the Set-DlpComplianceRule to modify data loss prevention (DLP) rules ... The EndpointDlpRestrictions parameter specifies the restricted endpoints for Endpoint DLP. ... @{"Setting"="RemovableMedia"; "Value"="Block";}

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: EndpointDlpRestrictions setting names include Print, RemovableMedia and NetworkShare.
claims.quote: @{"Setting"="Print"; "Value"="Block"} ... @{"Setting"="RemovableMedia"; "Value"="Block";} ... @{"Setting"="NetworkShare"; "Value"="Block";}

claims.where: Governance controls
claims.claim: Using Block or Warn with EndpointDlpRestrictions also requires NotifyUser.
claims.quote: When you use the values Block or Warn in this parameter, also need to use the NotifyUser parameter.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout, second bullet
claims.claim: The checklist directs administrators to check user and device policy scope, but no controls-table row governs that scope.
claims.quote: Check that the users and devices you expect are both in each rule's scope ...; controls rows: Whether a device rule audits, warns or blocks printing and copying to USB or network shares; Separate switch for protection of unsaved content.
claims.fix: Remove the Before rollout bullet beginning 'Check that the users and devices you expect are both in each rule's scope'. User/device policy scoping has no corresponding control row; the verified scope requirement can remain in Scope and the existing control's note.
